prompt.context_jp: その家で留守番をしているの___、幼い蒼穹と、テーコー不動産の若手営業マン・庭野聖司だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その家で留守番をしているの___、幼い蒼穹と、…庭野聖司だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that identifies WHO it was that was house-sitting.

feedback.correct_en: The 「〜のは…だった」 cleft pattern uses は to set up 'the one who was X' as the topic, then identifies the answer. The focus is on identifying who, not introducing new info out of the blue.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like brand-new information being asserted mid-stream; を is ungrammatical here because 留守番をしているの is a nominalised subject, not an object.

contrast_examples.jp: ここにいるのは私だけだ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who is here is only me.

prompt.context_jp: それでも少年の顔はほとんど笑わず、命令する声だけ___部屋に響いている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 命令する声だけ___部屋に響いている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'only the commanding voice echoed in the room.'

feedback.correct_en: The 'commanding voice' is new, perceptible information filling the scene — classic descriptive が. The contrast with the boy's unsmiling face makes this noun phrase the newly spotlighted subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 命令する声 into a known topic, which clashes with the fresh sensory description. を would require a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.jp: その声はもう聞こえない。
contrast_examples.en: That voice is no longer heard (known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外では、庭のびわの木___静かに枝を揺らしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 庭のびわの木___静かに枝を揺らしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing the loquat tree as a scenic subject.

feedback.correct_en: This is a 'camera pans and shows' description — が introduces the loquat tree as newly-noticed scenery. Narrative scene-setting with sensory verbs like 揺らしていた typically takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the tree a prior topic under discussion, which it isn't here — it is being presented. も implies 'also,' which has no antecedent.

contrast_examples.en: As for that tree, my father planted it.

prompt.context_jp: 「おばあちゃん___死んでない！」
prompt.prompt_jp: おばあちゃん___死んでない！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in Aoki's protest: 'Grandma hasn't died!'

feedback.correct_en: は carries a contrastive 'as for Grandma — she hasn't died (whatever you say).' It picks Grandma out against the implication others have accepted. Negative predicates often attract contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like identifying who died ('Grandma is the one who hasn't died'), which doesn't fit his emotional denial. も would absurdly add Grandma to a list.

prompt.context_jp: そこにいたの___、無表情のままこちらを見つめる三軒家万智だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこにいたの___、…三軒家万智だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the cleft: 'The one who stood there was Sangenya.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜のは〜だ cleft: the presupposed description ('the one who was there') takes は, and the identified answer (三軒家) follows. は sets the frame; だった gives the identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn 'the one who was there' into brand-new info, undermining the cleft structure. も implies 'also there,' not supported.

prompt.context_jp: 蒼穹の目から、こらえていた涙___ぼろぼろとこぼれ落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: こらえていた涙___ぼろぼろとこぼれ落ちた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'the tears he had been holding back spilled out.'

feedback.correct_en: The tears are an emergent, newly observed subject of an involuntary action (こぼれ落ちる). Spontaneous occurrence verbs take が on their emergent subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the tears a known topic — but we're seeing them appear for the first time in the narrative. を doesn't fit the intransitive こぼれ落ちる.

prompt.context_jp: 蒼穹___まだ、祖母の死を受け入れられずにいるのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蒼穹___まだ、祖母の死を受け入れられずにいるのだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Aoki as the sentence topic.

feedback.correct_en: Aoki is the established referent; the narrator comments on his ongoing state. 'As for Aoki — he still can't accept it.' This is classic topic は with a descriptive stative predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present him as newly identified, but he's been the focus for several lines. に doesn't mark the experiencer here.

prompt.context_jp: 両親がそろって病院に詰めているあいだ、蒼穹の相手___するのが庭野の役目になっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蒼穹の相手___するのが庭野の役目になっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'take care of (lit. do the companion role of) Aoki.'

feedback.correct_en: 相手をする is a set 'noun+を+する' collocation meaning 'to keep company / deal with.' を marks the direct object of する.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 相手 the subject of する, which doesn't fit this idiom. に would mean 'to the companion,' not idiomatic.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家はその隣___立ち、少年と同じ高さに視線を落とした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三軒家はその隣___立ち、…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'stood next to him.'

feedback.correct_en: 立つ meaning 'take a standing position' uses に to mark the location where the person comes to be — a result-location, not an activity site.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the site of an action in progress, but 立つ here is 'come to stand,' which pairs with に. を doesn't fit intransitive 立つ.

contrast_examples.en: To talk at the entrance (activity site).

prompt.context_jp: その頃、三軒家はひとり、夜の街___歩いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夜の街___歩いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'walked through the night streets.'

feedback.correct_en: Motion verbs like 歩く/走る/飛ぶ use を to mark the path/space traversed. 街を歩く = 'walk through/along the streets.'
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mean 'to the streets' (destination), losing the sense of traversal. で would mark a static activity location without the sense of movement through.

prompt.context_jp: 「あっ！ 僕の絵___！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕の絵___！
prompt.prompt_en: Aoki, pointing at the wall: 'That's MY drawing!' Choose the particle.

choices.text: だ (plain copula, with implied が)

feedback.correct_en: The exclamation identifies the referent on the spot: 'This = my drawing!' In Japanese, pointing-out identification often drops any particle after 僕の絵 and uses the copula directly (equivalent to これが僕の絵だ, exhaustive-listing が underneath).
feedback.incorrect_en: Adding は would make it a topic ('as for my drawing…'), losing the sudden-recognition punch. も ('also') would need something to add to.

prompt.context_jp: 坂の下に見えるその建物___、夫妻が毎日通う職場そのものだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 坂の下に見えるその建物___、…職場そのものだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'that building was their very workplace.'

feedback.correct_en: The building has just been pointed at in the previous line, so it's already established. The narrator now comments on it: 'as for that building, it was none other than their workplace.' Topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce it as new information, which clashes with the prior line. に has no role here.

contrast_examples.en: There's a shop over there (new info).

prompt.context_jp: 坂道を全力で駆け上がってきたの___、庭野だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 坂道を全力で駆け上がってきたの___、庭野だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the cleft 'The one who came running up the hill was Niwano.'

feedback.correct_en: Standard 〜のは〜だった cleft: the described-but-unnamed runner is the topic (は), and Niwano is the identifying predicate. The pattern mirrors sentence 0030.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the whole clause fresh news instead of a cleft identification. も has no 'also' basis.

contrast_examples.en: The one who was late is me.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が決意する時のつぶやき、そして契約成立後の心の声。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___」/「《___た》」(三軒家が客を契約まで導くことを意味する動詞)
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb does Sangenya use to mean 'secure a sale / close the client'?

choices.text: 捕まえる / 捕まった

feedback.correct_en: 落とす is sales-jargon (originally from courtship/persuasion) meaning 'to win over, to close.' 落ちた is the paired intransitive: 'they fell for it / they're sold.' This is the show's signature line.
feedback.incorrect_en: 倒す means 'to defeat/topple' — too combative. 捕まえる means 'to catch' — too literal and wrong register for closing a deal.

prompt.context_jp: 母親のために取っておいたのだろうと思うと、庭野は胸___詰まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 庭野は胸___詰まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes the emotional idiom 'his chest ___ got tight / he was overcome with emotion.'

feedback.correct_en: 胸が詰まる is a fixed emotional idiom: 'to be choked up / overcome with feeling.' The chest is the subject of the involuntary tightening.
feedback.incorrect_en: 胸を詰まる is ungrammatical (詰まる is intransitive). 胸に詰まる would require a thing that fills the chest.

contrast_examples.en: A feeling that chokes you up.
A bone gets stuck in the throat.

prompt.context_jp: 子供の機嫌を___ないようにすることが、今日の自分に課された最大の仕事だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 子供の機嫌を___ないようにする
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 機嫌を〜 to mean 'not upset (the child's) mood.'

feedback.correct_en: 機嫌を損ねる is the standard collocation: 'to spoil / upset someone's mood.' 損ねる is transitive and pairs naturally with 機嫌.
feedback.incorrect_en: 壊れる is intransitive and doesn't collocate with 機嫌. 失くす means 'to lose (an object)' and sounds unidiomatic with 機嫌.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家はその焦りを___ように、一切の前置きを省いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 焦りを___ように
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'see through (someone's inner state).'

feedback.correct_en: 見透かす means 'to see through' someone's thoughts or feelings — exactly fitting Sangenya reading the couple's impatience.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見下す means 'to look down on / despise.' 見送る means 'to see off / let pass,' neither fits 'read the impatience.'

contrast_examples.en: Look down on the other person.

prompt.context_jp: 家の中を駆け回る少年に、庭野は___も___も出ない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 庭野は___も___も出ない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'completely unable to handle the situation.'

feedback.correct_en: 手も足も出ない is a fixed idiom: 'can't lift a hand or a foot' = utterly helpless. It perfectly captures Niwano's inability to control the rampaging child.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other combinations are not idiomatic Japanese — they are literal body-part pairings that native speakers would not recognize as expressions.

contrast_examples.jp: 相手が強すぎて手も足も出ない。
contrast_examples.en: The opponent is too strong — I'm helpless.

prompt.context_jp: 部下を潰さないようにすることと数字を上げることの___に、屋代はほとほと疲れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 〜ことと〜ことの___に
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression meaning 'caught between two pressures.'

feedback.correct_en: 板挟み literally 'squeezed between two boards' describes being torn between two conflicting demands — perfect for a middle manager pressured from above and below.
feedback.incorrect_en: 押し付け means 'imposing' something on someone — one-way, not caught-between. 引き分け is 'a draw/tie' in competition, wrong register and meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 上司と部下の板挟みになる。
contrast_examples.en: Be caught between boss and subordinate.

prompt.context_jp: 嫌な___が、背筋をひやりと撫でた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 嫌な___が、背筋をひやりと撫でた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'premonition / bad feeling.'

feedback.correct_en: 嫌な予感 'a bad premonition' is the standard phrase for an uneasy foreboding. The chill-down-the-spine imagery matches a sudden intuition.
feedback.incorrect_en: 予定 is 'schedule/plan' — logically wrong. 予約 is 'reservation' — also wrong semantic field.

prompt.context_jp: 子供の扱いに慣れない庭野は、ただ___するばかりだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ただ___するばかりだった
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the mimetic word meaning 'flustered, at a loss.'

feedback.correct_en: おろおろする = 'to fluster, be at a loss' — exactly captures Niwano's panicked helplessness with an unhappy child.
feedback.incorrect_en: のろのろ = 'sluggishly slow'; ごろごろ = 'rumbling / lazing about.' Neither fits a flustered reaction.

contrast_examples.jp: 事故を見ておろおろする。
contrast_examples.en: Panic at the sight of an accident.

prompt.context_jp: Sangenya explains to the clients why Niwano isn't with her.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds like Sangenya's characteristic blunt business speech (A matches the story)?

choices.text: 庭野は役に立ちませんので 置いてきました
庭野さんは少しお役に立たないかもしれないので、申し訳ないのですが置いてきてしまいました

feedback.correct_en: Option A is the actual line: the humble-form 〜ので plus the blunt verdict 役に立ちません captures Sangenya's trademark polite-yet-ruthless register.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B over-softens with さん, 少し, 申し訳ない — natural Japanese, but completely out of character for Sangenya's cold, declarative style.

contrast_examples.jp: 役に立ちませんので置いてきました。
contrast_examples.en: He's useless, so I left him behind.

contrast_examples.jp: 少しお役に立たないかもしれません。
contrast_examples.en: He might be a bit unhelpful (over-polite hedging).

prompt.context_jp: Sangenya declares that this apartment is the best choice.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as Sangenya's closing recommendation?

choices.text: ここが 最高だと思います
ここは最高を思いますと

feedback.correct_en: Option A uses が to single out 'this place' as the uniquely best choice — natural identificational focus — plus the correct 〜だと思います complement order.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B has the quoted content 最高 bare (missing だ) and reverses 思います/と, which is ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.jp: ここが最高だと思います。
contrast_examples.en: I think this one is the best.
I think this one is number one.

prompt.context_jp: Sangenya tells the parents the hospital is so close the child can feel their presence.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'can sense the parents nearby'?

choices.text: 近くに ご両親を感じることが できる
近くで ご両親に感じることが できる

feedback.correct_en: 感じる 'to feel/sense' takes the thing felt as a direct object with を: ご両親を感じる = 'sense (the presence of) one's parents.' 近くに marks where they are.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B puts ご両親 with に (as if parents are the sense target the way あなたに感じる works), which is unidiomatic for perceiving someone's presence.

contrast_examples.jp: そばに人の気配を感じる。

prompt.context_jp: Sangenya warns Mika not to celebrate too soon after just getting a viewing appointment.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Sangenya's rebuke?

choices.text: はしゃぐのは早すぎる
はしゃぐことは早いすぎる

feedback.correct_en: 〜のは早すぎる is the natural pattern: the nominaliser の + topic は + stem+すぎる on the i-adjective 早い (drop the い).
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B uses こと (less natural for immediate judgment of an action) and keeps 早い+すぎる with the い, which is ungrammatical — すぎる attaches to the stem.

contrast_examples.en: It's too early to give up.

contrast_examples.jp: この問題は難しすぎる。

prompt.context_jp: Sangenya cuts off Yashiro's sympathy for Mika with a brutal rhetorical question.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line captures Sangenya's cold logic most naturally?

choices.text: 泣けば 家は売れるんですか？
泣いたら家が売れますでしょうか？

feedback.correct_en: Option A uses the sharp conditional 〜ば plus topic-contrastive は on 家, driving home 'as for houses — do they sell by crying?' The 〜んですか adds confrontational demand for explanation.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B's 〜たら and over-polite でしょうか soften the barb into a gentle inquiry — natural Japanese, but entirely wrong for Sangenya's icy tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 泣けば問題は解決するんですか？
泣いたら気持ちが楽になるかもしれません。
contrast_examples.en: Crying might make you feel better (soft).
